label: Aristotle, Physics VI.9, 240a1-17: Zeno's stadium argument is unsound: it rests on the false…
interpretation: Aristotle calls the stadium reasoning a paralogism and traces it to the false moving-versus-stationary equal-time premise; the formal claim concerns soundness (the argument assumes a false premise; the Lean atom keeps the name StadiumInferenceValid), not the existence of the described rows.
